AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To quantify differences in active cervical range of motion (aCROM) between patients with neck pain and those without neck pain, in patients with whiplash-associated disorders (WADs) and nontraumatic neck pain, and in patients with acute complaints versus those with chronic complaints.

AbstractText.Label: DATA SOURCES
AbstractText.content: Seven bibliographic databases were searched from inception to April 2015. In addition, a manual search was performed.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY SELECTION
AbstractText.content: Full articles on a numerical comparison of aCROM in patients with neck pain and asymptomatic control persons of similar ages were included. Two reviewers independently selected studies and assessed risk of bias.

AbstractText.Label: DATA EXTRACTION
AbstractText.content: Two reviewers extracted the data. Pooled mean differences of aCROM were calculated using a random-effects model.

AbstractText.Label: DATA SYNTHESIS
AbstractText.content: The search yielded 6261 hits; 27 articles (2366 participants, 13 low risk of bias) met the inclusion criteria. The neck pain group showed less aCROM in all movement directions compared with persons without neck pain. Mean differences ranged from -7.04° (95% CI, -9.70° to -4.38°) for right lateral bending (11 studies) to -89.59° (95% CI, -131.67° to -47.51°) for total aCROM (4 studies). Patients with WADs had less aCROM than patients with nontraumatic neck pain. No conclusive differences in aCROM were found between patients with acute and patients with chronic complaints.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Patients with neck pain have a significantly decreased aCROM compared with persons without neck pain, and patients with WADs have less aCROM than those with nontraumatic neck pain.
